# A document that does every one of those things legally

Each thing below is one character, one directory or one pair of backticks away
from the fixture that breaks the rule, and every one of them has to pass. This
fixture is the one that decides whether anybody can live with the reader.

A link to a document that is there, written from this document's own directory:
[decisions/layering.md](decisions/layering.md).

The same target written from the repository root, which is the other convention
these documents use: [docs/decisions/layering.md](../docs/decisions/layering.md).

A link to a file at the repository root, reached the way a document in a
subdirectory has to reach it: [../NOTICE.md](../NOTICE.md).

A link out of this repository, which nothing here answers for:
[the standard's publisher](https://www.iso.org/standard/no-such-thing.html).

A link to a place inside this document, which names no file at all:
[the section above](#a-document-that-does-every-one-of-those-things-legally).

A link to a heading inside another document, where the fragment is not part of
the file name: [layering](decisions/layering.md#what-this-costs).

A directory rather than a file, which exists and which git tracks no entry for:
[decisions](decisions).

A backticked path that is there, written from the repository root:
`cmd/gate/references.go`.

A backticked token with a slash and no extension, which is a directory and not a
claim about a file: `store/testdata`.

A backticked token with a slash that is a symbol rather than a path, which is
how this project writes a quantity: `L_n/L_nw`.

A backticked placeholder, which names a shape rather than a file:
`store/check/<id>.md`.

A backticked pattern, which is a glob and not a path: `**/testdata/byte-exact/*`.

A glob that does end in an extension, which is the one the star has to be
excluded for: `cmd/gate/testdata/*/the-near-miss.md`.

The same for the single-character wildcard: `cmd/gate/testdata/references/the-near-mis?.md`.

A backticked absolute path, which names a place on one machine and resolves for
nobody else: `D:/build/schallweg/docs/layout.md`.

A backticked path with a line number after it, which is quoted output and whose
file is in the tree: `cmd/gate/main.go:1`.

A fenced block full of paths that were true when the command ran, none of which
this reader may read:

```
$ git grep -n 'a rule that has moved' -- docs/
docs/gone/removed-in-an-earlier-release.md:14:a rule that has moved
$ ls /tmp/schallweg-gate-build-4021/no-such-thing
```

A path in an indented block, which is the other way this repository quotes a
command:

    $ cat docs/never-existed.md
